gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns an invalid interpolation estimate caused by using the seminorm in place of the full H1 norm for arbitrary errors, with a near-constant-error counterexample. ISSUE-001 instead diagnoses a separate supremum-versus-endpoint/integral inference in an abstract Gronwall continuation argument; it does not recognize the interpolation, mean, or nonlinear energy-estimate defect.

The gold issue is that point evaluation is not a well-defined operation on L2 equivalence classes and must be replaced by cell averages. ISSUE-001 concerns a factor-of-two error in a temporal supremum estimate and contains no diagnosis of representative dependence, point sampling, or initialization.

The gold issue concerns the underdetermined vector elliptic problem used to certify the gradient maximum norm and the missing boundary conditions and residuals. ISSUE-003 instead identifies an incorrectly signed first-time-slab convective residual term; it does not address the vector problem, its uniqueness, or certification of the gradient.

The gold issue is the unsupported extension of smooth-boundary existence results to the polygonal and mixed-boundary domain class. ISSUE-001 concerns an incorrect quantitative Gronwall factor in stability estimates and does not diagnose the missing local well-posedness or domain-regularity result.

The gold issue is circularity: the stability estimate is applied assuming existence through T even though existence through T is the conclusion to be certified, requiring localization below T_max and a continuation argument. ISSUE-001 only identifies a factor-of-two error in a different Gronwall bound and does not recognize the circular existence hypothesis or maximal-interval logic.
